Candidate pairs from a near-miss name inside a geographic block

Source: R/fuzzy.R
pf_fuzzy_candidates.Rd

Jaro-Winkler similarity on name_key within an exact ZIP5 block, falling back to city plus state where the ZIP5 block is empty. Blocking first is what makes this affordable: the pools are small (median 477 reference rows on the NO sample, largest 2,940) and scoring one takes microseconds, against the 223,151 candidates pass B2 generates on 5,000 grants.

Usage

pf_fuzzy_candidates(
  query,
  reference,
  cutoff = 0.9,
  top_k = 5L,
  block = c("zip5", "city_state"),
  personal = NULL,
  skip_personal = TRUE,
  max_pool = 20000L,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

query

A normalized query frame (from npmatch::np_normalize()) carrying name_key, zip5, city and state.

reference

A normalized reference frame with the same four columns.

cutoff

Minimum Jaro-Winkler similarity. Read the section above before lowering it.

top_k

Most candidates to emit per query row.

block

Which blocks to try, in order. "city_state" is a fallback for a query row whose ZIP5 matches no reference row (6 of 91 on the NO sample), not an additional pass: a row the ZIP5 block resolved is not retried.

personal

Optional logical vector, one per query row, from looks_personal on the prepared grants. Passed positionally, the same way pf_add_recovery_keys() takes only_truncated.

skip_personal

Drop query rows flagged personal before scoring.

max_pool

Refuse to score a block larger than this, and say so. A guard against a degenerate key – an all-blank ZIP5 column collapsing the whole reference into one block – not a tuning parameter.

verbose

Report pool sizes and how many pairs were emitted.

Value

An np_blocks frame of .x / .y indices, with a sim attribute holding the similarity of each emitted pair.

On the cutoff

The default of 0.90 is set from measurement, not taste. Scoring all 91 cases of the NO sample against their own ZIP5 pools:

  • 0.90 recovers 7 of the 33 identities the BMF does hold, and offers exactly one row across the 57 it does not – SEE SCHEDULE ATTACHED against SEE SCHEDULE O, which the placeholder filter below removes.

  • 0.85 recovers 11 of the 33, four more, but the highest-scoring personal name sits at 0.848: ALEXANDER SCHWEIG against ALEXANDER GRAHAM BELL ASSOCIATION. A one-point margin on 38 individuals is not a margin.

That near-collision is structural rather than bad luck. Jaro-Winkler's prefix bonus is exactly what rewards a shared first name, so individuals are the population this comparator is worst at excluding, and skip_personal exists to keep them out of the pool rather than leaving the cutoff to catch them.

See also

pf_fuzzy_recover(), pf_staged_passes()
